theme: Mountains & Peaks: The Himalayas, Andes & Alpinism
title: Mountains & Peaks: The Himalayas, Andes & Alpinism
description: Comprehensive 60-question high-altitude odyssey exploring the 14 Eight-Thousanders, the Seven Summits, iconic alpine ascents, and mountain geology.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain peak in the Western and Southern Hemispheres, rising to 6,961 meters in the Argentine Andes?
questions.explanation: Aconcagua in Mendoza Province, Argentina, is the highest summit on Earth outside the mountain ranges of Central and South Asia.

questions.question: Which colossal Alaskan peak is the highest mountain summit in North America, formerly known as Mount McKinley?
questions.explanation: Denali rises 6,190 meters above sea level and features one of the greatest base-to-peak vertical land rises of any mountain on Earth.

questions.question: What dormant stratovolcano in Tanzania is the highest freestanding mountain above surrounding terrain on Earth?
questions.explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro rises 5,895 meters above sea level with three volcanic cones named Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira.

questions.question: Which twin-peaked dormant volcano in the Caucasus Mountains of Russia is the highest peak in Europe at 5,642 meters?
questions.explanation: Mount Elbrus in the western Caucasus surpasses Mont Blanc by nearly a thousand meters to claim the European Seven Summit title.

questions.question: What remote peak in the Sentinel Range is the highest mountain summit on the continent of Antarctica?
questions.explanation: Mount Vinson rises 4,892 meters above sea level roughly 1,200 kilometers from the South Pole.

questions.question: What is the official height in meters above sea level of Aconcagua, the highest mountain summit outside Asia?
questions.explanation: Aconcagua in the Argentine Andes stands at 6,961 meters, making it the crowning peak of the Americas.

questions.question: Which formidable mountain on the China-Pakistan border is the second-tallest peak on Earth and known as the Savage Mountain?
questions.explanation: K2 in the Karakoram Range rises 8,611 meters and is notorious for severe weather, technical difficulty, and extreme fatality rates.

questions.question: What is the third-highest mountain in the world, situated along the sovereign border between Nepal and the Indian state of Sikkim?
questions.explanation: Kangchenjunga stands at 8,586 meters and was believed to be the highest mountain on Earth until the Great Trigonometrical Survey of the 1850s.

questions.question: Which eight-thousander peak is directly connected to Mount Everest via the famous South Col ridge at 7,986 meters?
questions.explanation: Lhotse is the fourth-highest mountain on Earth at 8,516 meters, sharing the standard South Col route with Mount Everest.

questions.question: Which distinct four-sided pyramid peak located twenty kilometers east of Mount Everest is the fifth-highest mountain on Earth?
questions.explanation: Makalu rises 8,485 meters and is recognized for its knife-edge ridges and challenging granite summit pyramid.

questions.question: What is the only 8,000-meter peak located entirely within Chinese Tibetan territory without bordering Nepal or Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Shishapangma rises 8,027 meters in south-central Tibet and was the final eight-thousander to be summited in 1964.

questions.question: What is the exact official height in meters above sea level of K2, the Savage Mountain?
questions.explanation: K2 stands at exactly 8,611 meters in the Karakoram Range, second only to Mount Everest.

questions.question: Which mountaineering duo achieved the historic first confirmed summit of Mount Everest on May 29, 1953?
questions.explanation: New Zealander Edmund Hillary and Nepali Sherpa Tenzing Norgay climbed the South Col route as part of the ninth British Everest expedition.

questions.question: What was the very first 8,000-meter mountain ever successfully climbed by humans, summited by a French expedition in 1950?
questions.explanation: Maurice Herzog and Louis Lachenal reached the 8,091-meter summit of Annapurna I on June 3, 1950, without bottled oxygen.

questions.question: Which legendary Italian mountaineer became the first person to climb all fourteen 8,000-meter peaks without supplemental oxygen?
questions.explanation: Reinhold Messner completed all fourteen eight-thousanders between 1970 and 1986, establishing new benchmarks in alpine-style climbing.

questions.question: Which mountain in Pakistan earned the grim nickname Killer Mountain after thirty-one climbers died before its first ascent in 1953?
questions.explanation: Nanga Parbat at 8,126 meters features the Rupal Face, the highest vertical mountain face in the world rising 4,600 meters.

questions.question: Who was the first woman in history to stand atop the summit of Mount Everest, achieving the feat in May 1975?
questions.explanation: Japanese mountaineer Junko Tabei reached the summit via the South Col route, leading an all-female expedition.

questions.question: In what year did Maurice Herzog and Louis Lachenal reach the summit of Annapurna, completing the first ascent of an 8,000-meter peak?
questions.explanation: The French expedition stood on the summit of Annapurna on June 3, 1950, ushering in the golden age of Himalayan mountaineering.

questions.question: Because of Earth equatorial bulge, the summit of which Ecuadorian volcano is the closest terrestrial point to the Moon and outer space?
questions.explanation: Chimborazo summit sits 6,384 kilometers from Earth center, roughly two kilometers farther from the core than Mount Everest.

questions.question: What is the highest active volcano on Earth, rising to 6,893 meters along the border between Chile and Argentina?
questions.explanation: Ojos del Salado in the Atacama region is the highest volcano on Earth and the second-highest peak in the Western Hemisphere.

questions.question: Which perfectly symmetrical snow-capped stratovolcano is one of the highest active volcanoes in the world, located south of Quito?
questions.explanation: Cotopaxi stands at 5,897 meters and is sacred in indigenous Andean culture, renowned for its almost perfect cone profile.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain summit in Peru, located in the Cordillera Blanca range of the central Andes at 6,768 meters?
questions.explanation: Mount Huascarán is the highest tropical mountain on Earth, protected inside the UNESCO-listed Huascarán National Park.

questions.question: Which jagged granite monolith in Patagonia on the Argentina-Chile border is named after the captain of HMS Beagle?
questions.explanation: Mount Fitz Roy, also known as Chaltén, was named by explorer Francisco Moreno in honor of Captain Robert FitzRoy.

questions.question: What is the official elevation in meters above sea level of Ojos del Salado, the world highest volcano?
questions.explanation: Nevado Ojos del Salado stands at 6,893 meters in the dry Andes, featuring a permanent crater lake near its summit.

questions.question: What iconic pyramid-shaped peak on the Swiss-Italian border was first climbed in 1865 by an expedition led by Edward Whymper?
questions.explanation: The first ascent of the 4,478-meter Matterhorn on July 14, 1865, ended in tragedy when four climbers fell to their deaths during the descent.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain peak in the Alps and Western Europe, rising on the border between France and Italy?
questions.explanation: Mont Blanc stands at approximately 4,808 meters, first summited in 1786 by Jacques Balmat and Michel Paccard.

questions.question: Which mountain in the Bernese Alps is notorious for its sheer, 1,800-meter-high North Face nicknamed the Nordwand or Murder Wall?
questions.explanation: The Eiger North Face was considered the most formidable climbing problem in the Alps until it was conquered by a four-man team in 1938.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain peak in Austria, rising to 3,798 meters in the High Tauern range along the Grossglockner High Alpine Road?
questions.explanation: Grossglockner is a pyramid-shaped twin peak first climbed in 1800 by a team organized by Prince-Bishop Salm-Reifferscheidt.

questions.question: Which mountain in the Julian Alps is the highest peak and national symbol of Slovenia, featured on the Slovenian national flag?
questions.explanation: Triglav rises 2,864 meters and features three distinct crests, with the iconic Aljaž Tower erected on its summit in 1895.

questions.question: What is the official measured elevation in meters of Mont Blanc, the highest summit in the Alps?
questions.explanation: Mont Blanc measured height fluctuates slightly with summit ice pack depth, officially recorded at approximately 4,808 meters.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain peak in Canada and second-highest in North America, located in Kluane National Park in Yukon?
questions.explanation: Mount Logan rises 5,959 meters and boasts the largest base circumference of any non-volcanic mountain on Earth.

questions.question: Which massive glaciated stratovolcano in Washington State is the most topographically prominent mountain in the contiguous United States?
questions.explanation: Mount Rainier rises 4,392 meters and is encased in twenty-six major glaciers, looming prominently over the Seattle metropolitan area.

questions.question: What is the highest summit in the contiguous United States, rising to 4,421 meters in the Sierra Nevada range of California?
questions.explanation: Mount Whitney lies just 136 kilometers west of Badwater Basin in Death Valley, the lowest point in North America.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain peak in the Rocky Mountains system, rising to 4,401 meters in the Sawatch Range of Colorado?
questions.explanation: Mount Elbert is the highest of Colorado fifty-eight fourteeners, featuring a gentle ascent trail compared to technical peaks.

questions.question: Which peak in Wyoming is the signature mountain of Grand Teton National Park, rising dramatically without foothills above Jackson Hole?
questions.explanation: Grand Teton rises 4,199 meters as a classic glaciated horn, first officially summited in 1898 by Franklin Spalding and team.

questions.question: What is the official summit elevation in meters above sea level of Denali in Alaska?
questions.explanation: The United States Geological Survey established the official height of Denali at 6,190 meters following high-precision GPS surveys in 2015.

questions.question: What is the second-highest mountain summit in Africa, featuring dramatic twin volcanic peaks named Batian and Nelion?
questions.explanation: Mount Kenya rises 5,199 meters as an extinct stratovolcano whose glaciers feed vital water systems across central Kenya.

questions.question: Which mountain range along the Uganda-DRC border was identified by Ptolemy as the legendary snow-capped Mountains of the Moon?
questions.explanation: The Rwenzori Mountains host Mount Stanley at 5,109 meters and are one of only three glaciated mountain ranges in Africa.

questions.question: What is the highest island peak on Earth, rising 4,884 meters in the Sudirman Range on the island of New Guinea?
questions.explanation: Puncak Jaya, also known as Carstensz Pyramid, is the highest peak in Oceania and the highest summit between the Himalayas and the Andes.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain summit on the mainland Australian continent, located in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales?
questions.explanation: Mount Kosciuszko stands at 2,228 meters, named in 1840 by Polish explorer Paweł Strzelecki in honor of military hero Tadeusz Kościuszko.

questions.question: What active stratovolcano on the island of Java is known as the highest mountain on the island, rising to 3,676 meters?
questions.explanation: Mount Semeru is an active volcano that produces regular ash plumes and is revered in Javanese Hindu-Buddhist cosmology as Mahameru.

questions.question: What is the summit elevation in meters of Mount Kilimanjaro Uhuru Peak in Tanzania?
questions.explanation: Uhuru Peak on the Kibo crater rim of Mount Kilimanjaro stands at exactly 5,895 meters above sea level.

questions.question: In high-altitude mountaineering, what critical altitude threshold marks the beginning of the physiological Death Zone?
questions.explanation: Above 8,000 meters, atmospheric pressure drops to about one-third of sea level, preventing the human body from acclimatizing.

questions.question: How many official mountain peaks on Earth surpass the 8,000-meter threshold above sea level?
questions.explanation: All fourteen eight-thousanders are located in the Himalayan and Karakoram ranges of Central and South Asia.

questions.question: What distinct geological limestone formation sits near the very summit of Mount Everest, proving the peak was once an ancient seafloor?
questions.explanation: Marine fossils including ordovician trilobites and crinoids have been discovered embedded in the limestone near Everest summit.

questions.question: Which technical granite summit in the Karakoram is named for its massive, one-and-a-half-kilometer-long summit ridge at 8,051 meters?
questions.explanation: Broad Peak, originally designated K3, was first climbed in 1957 by an Austrian team using pure alpine style without supplemental oxygen.

questions.question: What is the steep rock step on the Northeast Ridge of Mount Everest that forms the most famous technical obstacle on the Tibetan route?
questions.explanation: The Second Step features a near-vertical thirty-meter rock wall at 8,610 meters, now equipped with a famous aluminum ladder installed in 1975.

questions.question: How many mountain peaks on Earth are officially classified as Eight-Thousanders, rising above 8,000 meters in elevation?
questions.explanation: There are precisely 14 independent summits on Earth that exceed 8,000 meters above sea level.

questions.question: When measured from its underwater base on the Pacific Ocean floor to its summit, what is the tallest mountain on Earth?
questions.explanation: Mauna Kea stands 4,207 meters above sea level, but extends nearly six thousand meters beneath the ocean surface for over 10,200 meters total height.

questions.question: Which sacred Japanese stratovolcano is celebrated as an exceptional cultural and spiritual icon, rising to 3,776 meters on Honshu?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji is the highest peak in Japan and one of Japan Three Holy Mountains, renowned for its symmetrical snow-draped volcanic cone.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain peak in Spain, situated on the volcanic island of Tenerife in the Canary Islands?
questions.explanation: Mount Teide rises 3,715 meters above sea level and casts the world largest sea shadow across the Atlantic Ocean at sunrise.

questions.question: Which active Antarctic volcano features a persistent convecting phonolitic lava lake in its summit caldera?
questions.explanation: Mount Erebus on Ross Island is the southernmost active volcano on Earth, discovered in 1841 by Sir James Clark Ross.

questions.question: Which Cascade Range stratovolcano underwent a catastrophic lateral blast eruption on May 18, 1980, lowering its summit by 400 meters?
questions.explanation: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake triggered the largest landslide in recorded history, unleashing a devastating pyroclastic blast across Washington State.

questions.question: What is the total base-to-peak height in meters of Mauna Kea from the oceanic trench floor to its summit?
questions.explanation: From its base on the Pacific Ocean floor at roughly 6,000 meters depth to its 4,207-meter summit, Mauna Kea spans roughly 10,210 meters total height.

questions.question: In 2019, which Nepali mountaineer shattered the world record by summiting all fourteen 8,000-meter peaks in just six months and six days?
questions.explanation: Nirmal Nimsdai Purja completed Project Possible 14/7, smashing the previous record of seven years and eleven months.

questions.question: Which mountain guide holds the world record for the highest number of successful summits of Mount Everest, having summited over thirty times?
questions.explanation: Kami Rita Sherpa set consecutive world records by guiding commercial and research expeditions to the summit of Everest year after year.

questions.question: In January 2021, an all-Nepali team achieved the historic and long-sought first winter ascent of which formidable mountain?
questions.explanation: Ten Nepali mountaineers united on the final ridge to reach the summit of K2 in sub-zero winter winds on January 16, 2021.

questions.question: Which British mountaineer famously replied 'Because it is there' when asked why he wanted to climb Mount Everest, before disappearing on the peak in 1924?
questions.explanation: George Mallory and Andrew Irvine vanished high on the Northeast Ridge on June 8, 1924, sparking mountaineering greatest enduring mystery.

questions.question: What is the classic high-altitude mountain sickness caused by rapid ascent to altitudes above 2,500 meters without proper acclimatization?
questions.explanation: Acute Mountain Sickness is caused by reduced atmospheric pressure and lower oxygen saturation, which can progress to life-threatening HAPE or HACE.

questions.question: In what year did Junko Tabei become the first woman in history to successfully stand on the summit of Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: Junko Tabei reached the summit of Mount Everest on May 16, 1975, via the South Col route alongside Sherpa Ang Tshering.
